titleStmt.title: Encyclopædia Britannica, Eleventh Edition — TEI customisation (ODD)

sourceDesc.p: Encyclopædia Britannica, 11th edition, Cambridge University Press, 1910–1911, transcribed at Wikisource and encoded from that transcription.

div.head: Scope
div.p: One TEI document per article — 37,225 of them — named by the article's stable identifier, which is also the tail of its URL at britannica11.org. teiCorpus is a catalogue binding them with XInclude; members are self-contained and are meant to be processed individually.

The encoding carries what the printed page carried and nothing more. There is no persName, placeName, orgName (in the text), date or other entity markup: the Encyclopædia does not mark its persons and places, so producing them would mean inferring them, and an inferred entity is an assertion in the editor's voice about a source that made no such claim.

div.head: Provenance is three-valued
div.p: The text is the Encyclopædia's; the transcription is the Wikisource contributors', credited in every respStmt; the encoding is this edition's. Where the transcribers added something the printed page does not contain — chiefly transliterations of Greek — it is carried as note with type transliteration and resp pointing at the Wikisource respStmt, so a consumer can tell the 1911 page from a later editor. Pages whose transcription is unproofread carry a warning in editorialDecl.

div.head: Presentation
div.p: Presentational distinctions the source makes are carried with rendition, declared once per document in tagsDecl, so the set is enumerable in the header rather than scattered through the corpus. Distinctions carrying a VALUE rather than a class — a font size, a line height, a transform — ride in style as CSS, because the value is the source's own and bucketing it would discard it.
The declared renditions are: sc (small capitals), bold, center, float-left, float-right, mirror, rule-block, rule-inline, bar, verse, sub, sup.

div.head: The elements used
div.p: Structure: TEI, teiHeader, fileDesc, titleStmt, title, author, respStmt, resp, orgName, publicationStmt, publisher, availability, licence, idno, sourceDesc, biblStruct, monogr, edition, imprint, pubPlace, date, biblScope, encodingDesc, projectDesc, editorialDecl, tagsDecl, rendition, revisionDesc, change, text, body, div, head, p.
Content: hi, emph, seg, lb, milestone, anchor, ref, note, formula, figure, graphic, table, row, cell, list, item, lg, l.

A div carries type entry for the article, section for a major division and subsection for a shoulder heading. A list carries type ordered or bulleted — whether a list is numbered is something the source states, not a rendition.

div.head: Identifiers
div.p: Every xml:id is unique WITHIN its document and not across the corpus: each member declares its own respStmt and its own renditions so that it can be read, validated and cited alone. Resolving every XInclude into a single tree therefore produces duplicate identifiers. Process members individually, or rewrite identifiers on assembly.
Section identifiers take the form section-slug, and are the same anchors the website uses, so a TEI identifier and a URL fragment name the same place.
